Michael Dobbs reported for the Washington Post in October 1991 that the spy war was ending. Yevgeny Primakov, the new Soviet spymaster, declared an end to the secret intelligence war with the United States. The KGB's long contest with American intelligence, Dobbs wrote, had fallen victim to glasnost.

An intelligence chief announcing peace in his secret war was a sign of how far the Soviet opening had gone. The statement came weeks before the Soviet Union itself dissolved. Dobbs's article preserves the moment the Cold War's hidden front was publicly stood down.
